question: What primary function does accounting serve in a healthcare facility?
explanation: Accounting focuses on tracking and summarizing money coming in and going out to maintain financial visibility. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h1)

question: Why is budgeting essential for a hospital ward manager?

options.A: It determines the medical diagnosis of patients
options.B: It eliminates all financial risks in a hospital
options.C: It replaces the need for clinical nursing protocols
options.D: It plans future income and expenses to guide care

explanation: A budget provides a roadmap for anticipating costs and allocating funds effectively for future ward operations. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h1)

question: Staff salaries and utility bills in a hospital are classified as which type of financial item?
explanation: Day-to-day running costs required to keep the facility functional are categorized as operating expenses. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h2)

question: A clinic purchases a brand-new standby generator for the theater. This purchase represents what kind of cost?
explanation: Major equipment purchases with long-term value are classified as capital costs rather than routine daily expenses. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h2)

question: Which budget category typically accounts for the largest share of expenses in a nursing department?
explanation: Salary and labor costs for nurses and other healthcare staff make up the bulk of daily operating expenses. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of a capital budget in a hospital setting?

options.D: Paying monthly electricity and water bills

explanation: Capital budgets are specifically designated for acquiring high-value, long-lasting assets like diagnostic machines. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h3)

question: When does the preparation for a new fiscal year's budget typically begin?

options.A: Months before the new fiscal year starts
options.B: On the very first day of the new year
options.C: Only after the fiscal year has ended
options.D: Whenever cash reserves run completely dry

explanation: Budget planning requires extensive forecasting and review, so it starts well in advance of the actual financial year. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h4)

question: Why must nurse managers submit input during the hospital budgeting cycle?

options.A: They decide the overall tax rates for the healthcare sector
options.B: They handle the direct collection of patient hospital bills
options.C: They are required by law to sign all bank documents
options.D: They understand the specific clinical needs of their units

explanation: Frontline managers provide accurate estimates of equipment and staffing needs based on actual patient care demands. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h4)

question: A ward manager notices high rates of expired IV infusion bags in the treatment room. What is the best immediate step for cost control?

options.A: Stop ordering all IV fluids for the entire hospital
options.B: Ignore the expired stock if the total cost is low
options.C: Ask patients to buy their own infusion stands
options.D: Improve inventory rotation and stock monitoring

explanation: Proper inventory management prevents financial loss from expired stock while ensuring necessary supplies remain usable. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h5)

question: How does poor staff scheduling impact the financial health of a nursing unit?

options.A: It guarantees an increase in annual government grants
options.B: It wastes funds on overstaffing or increases costly overtime
options.C: It eliminates the need for any future budget reviews
options.D: It automatically lowers the cost of hospital drugs

explanation: Inefficient scheduling leads to unnecessary expenditure either through idle excess staff or expensive emergency overtime. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h5)

question: What does a financial variance represent in a healthcare budget?

options.A: The total profit generated by a private clinic
options.B: The difference between budgeted and actual financial figures
options.C: The tax rate charged on imported medical equipment
options.D: The salary grade level of a senior nursing officer

explanation: Variance measures the gap between what was planned financially and what actually occurred in practice. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h6)

question: Why might a highly 'favorable' supply cost variance actually require investigation by a nurse manager?

options.A: It guarantees that the hospital will lose its operating license
options.B: It means the government has increased taxes on the ward
options.C: It always indicates that staff are stealing hospital medications
options.D: It might mean essential supplies were not ordered, risking care

explanation: While spending less looks good on paper, extreme underspending can mean patients went without needed medications or supplies. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of a financial audit in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To write new clinical guidelines for surgical wards
options.B: To diagnose complicated patient medical conditions
options.C: To assign duty rosters for junior nursing staff
options.D: To verify records, ensure compliance, and detect errors

explanation: Audits review financial documentation to confirm accuracy, prevent fraud, and ensure adherence to financial policies. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h7)

question: What does financial accountability mean for a practicing nurse manager?

options.A: Covering up budget shortfalls to avoid awkward meetings
options.B: Refusing to order any new equipment for the hospital ward
options.C: Taking responsibility for resource use and financial decisions
options.D: Leaving all money matters strictly to the bank accountants

explanation: Accountability requires managers to own the financial outcomes of their units and justify how resources are spent. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h7)
